Experiment 0 v3 — Scorer Validation (Definitive)

The Road to v3

Experiment 0 asks a simple question: which LLM judge most reliably tracks whether a RAG answer is actually correct? It took three iterations to get a confident answer.

v1 (n=50) was our first attempt. It had two critical flaws: judges scored against the full source document instead of the retrieved chunks the LLM actually saw, and there was no reranker in the pipeline. Sonnet came out on top — but the methodology was unsound.

v2 (n=150) fixed the tracking, added a BGE reranker (retrieve 10, keep 3), and filtered to medium+hard questions to avoid ceiling effects. Haiku beat Sonnet — directly contradicting v1. But with only 150 questions, the margin left room for doubt.

v3 (n=500) is the tiebreaker at scale. With 500 HotpotQA questions and 6 LLM judges (3 Gemini, 3 Claude), the results are clear: Claude Haiku is the most accurate judge (r=0.450 with gold F1), followed by Sonnet (0.397) and Opus (0.382). Among the free Gemini judges, Flash and Pro are nearly interchangeable (r=0.892). The question is settled.

Key Findings

v3 — 500 medium+hard HotpotQA questions, 6 LLM judges (3 Gemini + 3 Claude)

  • Best judge: Claude Haiku (r=0.450 gold F1)
  • Best free judge: Gemini 2.5 Pro (r=0.348)
  • Pipeline accuracy: 76.2% exact match, mean F1 0.546
  • Failure stages: 76% none, 14% retrieval, 10% generation
